claim_map.title: Preserving onboarding interfaces
claim_map.text: The proposal must preserve existing business functions and integrate unified maker/checker review. It moves branch-code configuration from application.yml to ratanone.branch_code_config and changes consumers to read the database.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.

claim_map.title: Ownership and one review flow
claim_map.text: The design proposes one form and one maker/checker operation across related static configuration. Its temporary conclusion assigns static-service maintenance and query responsibility. Alternatives using separate domain storage, events, or distributed transactions are comparison options, not selected parallel architectures.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.

claim_map.title: FAQ decisions and staged alternatives
claim_map.text: The FAQ selects one form and one review flow. It requests CRUD while keeping bookingEntityFmid immutable. It excludes historical-data migration and excludes Nostro from this self-service form. It proposes ACTIVE to SAVE_CONFIRMED conversion and deprecation of the old cutoff API. It selects merging SWIFT sender/correspondent tables and unified review. Currency mapping temporarily uses group-service, with later static-service migration. This staging differs from the main design target. Country-zone warmup must complete before accounting jobs run. These are design decisions, without inspected migration or execution.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.

claim_map.title: API design scope
claim_map.text: The API proposal uses POST /v1/onboard-config/draft, /submit, /update, /approve, /reject, /query, /delete, and /history. Draft saves to the database; submit starts review. Update starts from SAVE_CONFIRMED. Query supports statuses, pagination, and sorting. History uses mainTableId. The separate /v1/rounding-config family provides draft, submit, update, query, delete, bulk-approve, bulk-reject, and history. The rounding update example strikes out currency editing. Successful saves return 200; invalid parameters return 400; internal errors return 500 where specified. Example identifiers and history snapshots establish no grants, actual operations, or complete error contract.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.

claim_map.title: Business input and backend boundary
claim_map.text: The chosen UI uses a blotter and subtiles. Static Ops can edit; other users are read-only. FMID is numeric and immutable; FMCode is populated and immutable. Branch-code golden-source handling remains open. Currency mapping is a separate optional global blotter, with required precision and ROUNDING_OFF, ROUNDING_DOWN, or ROUNDING_UP. ISO mapping is optional. Release cutoff uses currency, GMT time, VD-2/VD-1/VD, and business-day default. Local-time conversion remains a question. SWIFT and accounting sections are optional when applicable. Backend teams retain MX bifurcation, new-country EBBS connectivity and jobs, CPT, and country-specific analysis.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.

claim_map.title: Conditional SWIFT and accounting fields
claim_map.text: Sender BIC and its editable country default belong to the SWIFT section. Field 53 uses an 8- or 11-character BIC for the stated OverAccount or NOS currency/message branches, with Nostro fallback. Field 58 BIC applies to MT202 Flip. Accounting captures bridge account, posting branch, transaction type, debit/credit codes, accounting country, and ZoneId. SWIFT country and accounting country remain distinct. Post-confirmed-update controls and backend suppression currency handling remain unresolved.
claim_map.confidence: high for bounded source-specific wording; current applicability unresolved
claim_map.rationale: Selected original text explicitly supplies this rule or labelled proposal; competing scope and omissions remain stated.
